newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU meet on Albania, Turkey, Burma.
newsitem.headline: EU meet on Albania, Turkey, Burma.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers began meeting on Monday to discuss the bloc's next move on Albania and to see if Greece would lift its objections to a long-delayed meeting with Turkey.
The ministers were also expected to strip Burma of special trading priveleges over concerns about humans rights in the country. The move was due to be rubber stamped without discussion.
On Albania, the ministers were to get a report from an EU mission to Tirana last week and to discuss whether conditions on the ground would now allow for humanitarian aid to be delivered.
EU Humanitarian Aid Commissioner Emma Bonino said last week that aid was ready but that some form of security structure had to be put in place before it could be delivered.

Attempts will also be made to hold an Association Council -- a formal EU meeting -- with Turkey on April 29 and 30. The meeting has been put off for more than a year as the result of Greek concerns about Turkish intentions in the Aegean.
At a meeting in Apeldoorn, the Netherlands, last weekend, the ministers tried to smooth over a row with Turkey about its eventual prospects to join the EU.
Centrist politicians had earlier caused a stir by seemingly ruling Ankaara out of membership.
The ministers will also discuss whether to put South Africa on a fast track to join the Lome Convention, the bloc's main treaty with the developing world.
Negotiations with Pretoria over a special trade pact have stalled and the Lome move is seen partially as a way of keeping them on track.
Spain, however, has blocked the move so far because it wants further progress on a fisheries agreement with South Africa first.
The ministerial meeting will end releatively early to allow the ministers to fly to Italy's capital for the 40th annniversary celebrations on Tuesday of the signing of the Treaty of Rome.
